ai.title: system-prompt.ts add terminal command file edit restriction
ai.summary: Added explicit instruction to system-prompt.ts prohibiting use of run_terminal_command for creating or editing files. Directs agent to use <file> blocks per editing_instructions instead. Affects backend prompt logic only.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant will no longer create or modify files using terminal commands. Instead, it will use its built-in file editing capabilities when changes to files are needed. This ensures file edits are handled through the proper interface rather than direct terminal access. The change only affects how the assistant interacts with the filesystem internally.

ai.title: Refine editing instructions in system prompt
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to clarify that edits are applied by a separate assistant, requiring explicit context and shorter excerpts. Added guidance to preserve user edits and avoid reproducing unchanged code sections. Updated `todo.knowledge.md` with a new item regarding tree-sitter integration.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to change part of a file, it now explains the change in shorter pieces and lets a separate helper apply the edit, rather than rewriting whole files and risking lost work. This mainly affects anyone who writes instructions for the assistant, since their wording now needs to be clearer and more focused. The change is live today, so you'll notice the assistant giving more targeted, step-by-step editing guidance during a session. A planning list also gained a reminder to try a specific code-analysis tool.
